Transnet, still in turmoil

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Transnet continues to create a major problem with ineffective Port Terminals, while transporters and exporters take the knock.

Unique Selling Point:
- A story we've covered before and followed over the years
- Exclusive audio clip of Transnet's Senior Operations Manager admitting to equipment failures

Summary:
In 2019 Joy produced Ports in Peril. In 2023, I produced Shipping Shambles. The central theme Transnet is costing the economy millions due to inefficiencies and equipment failures.

2025. Not much has changed. This time round, I have great clips and data from the transporters on the ground laying the blame squarely at Transnet’s door and we’ve got the evidence to back up these allegations.

Further information:
TRANSNET – BIG PROMISES & MASSIVE FAILURES


KEY POINTS
 The focus is Cape Town Port Terminal.
 7 secondhand RTGs purchased – only 2 working. In less than a year.
 A round trip for a transporter should take 40min-75 min. It’s taking between 5-10 hours, we have proof of a 2 day turn around. Video clips and port access slips.
 We have access to internal Transnet staff through one of the unions providing information.
 We have independent statistics showing a decrease in productivity.

In December 2023, Transnet announces that its bought 7 second Rubber Tyre Gantries (RTG) It promises to ease up the equipment failures and delays experienced in the port. BUT…. Wait for it…. The seven arrived from Los Angeles, without spares, without maintenance plan in place. And one of them was dead on arrival. The remaining 6 started operating in April 2024. Today, only two are operational.

WHAT DOES THIS MEAN
Delays in the port for transporters who carry the costs. SINCE January 2022, seven transporters have called it quits:
• Max Logistics
• TI Logistics
• Giovanni Logistics
• Conrad Logistics
• Olympic Trucking
• Container Domestic Services
• GT Trucking

These closures have led to job losses, financial ruin for business owners, and an increasingly unstable transport sector.

Issues with the booking system

WHERE DOES TRANSNET STAND ON ALL OF THIS
In November 2024 Transnet was quoted in Freight News Article:
“Transnet said since their deployment in December 2023, the RTGs had improved vessel turnaround times, with delays dropping from 300 hours to as little as 45 hours.
‘This improvement has been instrumental in reducing congestion and enhancing service delivery to customers. The terminal is now able to berth vessels on arrival, except during unavoidable weather delays,’ Transnet said.”

BUT TRANSNET STAFF ARE CALLING BULLSHIT
The United National Transport Union represents 55% of Transnet staff. They have sent me current data on break downs and non-operational equipment.

JUICY CLIP
I also have an audio recording from a stakeholders meeting held on 16 October 2024 where Ophelia Shabane, the Senior Operations Manager says the following:
“The RTGs that were procured, the secondhand RTGs have been the greatest disappointment for the Terminal. // in terms of their reliability they have not been reliable. // That is a known fact. // Those RTGS are in an even worse condition and breaking down even further than the ones we originally had.”

THE BIG QUESTION?
Who is being held responsible for this purchase – it’s impacted on Transnet operations, crippled transporters and affects SA’s export market when we can’t deliver.

WIND DOWN TIME
NOT APPLICABLE – the RTGs are responsible for the land

INTERVIEWS
- Transnet
- Transporter that closed down – Online Interview – Jet Pieters – he lives in Gansbaai
- Current Transporter
o Either SATA – an association representing some transport companies
o Or a hidden ID with a transport owner
- United National Transport Union – either the union rep – very well versed on the issues around the second hand RTGs or a hidden ID worker / mechanic person about first hand struggles
- Fruit Exporter - impacts

Script:


TRANSNET – BIG PROMISES & MASSIVE FAILURES

VO: The Port of Cape Town. Strategically positioned; perfectly situated to capitalize on international shipping trade.

But it’s not.

SEQUENCE OF CELLPHONE CLIPS
UPSOUND CLIP 1- SUBTITLES: Only one machine works over there.
UPSOUND CLIP 2 - SUBTITLES: There’s the other machine, it’s going to load a container now

VO: Constant delays are crippling businesses.

UPSOUND CELLPHONE CLIP - Right, this machine is broken, this one is broken again….

VO: Transnet's Port Terminal leadership though, appears to have a different view.

BORCHARDS: There's a progressive increase in productivity,

VO: …but the people on ground are far from convinced.

TRANSPORTER: there are good days, but they are more bad days than what they are good days.

AUDIO BEAT

LINK: There are three main reasons for the delays here at the Port of Cape Town the booking system. Perpetual closure due to wind and frequent equipment breakdowns. But none of these issues are unique to South Africa. so the problem may be within Transnet itself.

VO: This isn’t the first time we’ve shone a light on Transnet.

It’s an ongoing saga with a central theme, this state-owned entity is costing the economy billions due to security issues, inefficiencies and equipment failures.

And in 2025, not much has changed. This investigation will reveal how Transnet is trying to spin a dire situation.

LINK: So last night we heard that there were massive breakdowns inside the Cape Town harbour, forcing Transnet to shut the gates and trapping drivers inside after 2 a.m. and keeping other trucks out. And this morning, we're seeing the consequences. Those trucks are backed up all the way up to the bridge.

VO: There are two sides to port operations – the waterside where containers are loaded on and off ships, and the landside where trucks pick up and drop off the containers.

Transnet claims it’s turned a corner, but transporters aren’t buying it - they’re at a standstill.

DERICK: If they have it under control, why are we standing in long queues outside and inside the terminal? That's not, having it under control.

VO: Derick Ongansie represents the South African Transporters Alliance - he was an owner-driver for more than a decade, but called it quits four years ago.

DERICK: in 2021 I closed down because it was no longer profitable to serve as the port.
GOVAN: Is what happened to you an isolated case or has it happened to other transporters?
DERICK: //. There's more companies that that closed down // we’re talking about at least 200 trucks exiting the industry. // because of the long hours we spent in the queues inside the port and in the terminal.

VO: The constant breakdowns are mainly caused by old equipment. A key culprit is the ageing fleet of so-called Rubber Tyre Gantries, or RTGs.

These machines stack containers and move them to and from trucks, for transport in and out of the port - they’re the lifeblood of the port, essential for its proper functioning.

But with lead times of 18-24 months for new RTGs, Transnet opted to buy 7 secondhand machines. They arrived in December 2023, with a price tag of R140 million.

One, was dead on arrival, while the others were only operational by April 2024.

While, these are facts Transnet doesn’t dispute - it doesn’t seem bothered by them either.

Oscar Borchards is the Managing Executive for the Transnet Port Terminal in the Western Cape.

GOVAN: Did those second hand RTGs improve efficiency?
BORCHARDS: Yes it did.
GOVAN: Was the purchase of those RTGs a success?
BORCHARDS: It was.it brought in the redundancy for this terminal Without the seven RTGs, you would have been in the worst situation.

VO: But is that the case?

ATENKOSI: // So these RTG had problems from the start//

VO: Atenkosi Plaatjie is from the United National Transport Union or UNTU. She says the second-hand RTGs have regular breakdowns - when we spoke, only two were working.

ATENKOSI: we represent members that are on the ground that are working with the equipment on a daily basis. at the port of Cape Town

VO: UNTU maintains it was a knee-jerk order

ATENKOSI: Remember that you need the right specifications for the port. It's not a one size fits all.

VO: This is one of the pre-existing RTGS. This blue one is secondhand.

ATENKOSI: you can clearly see the white two white lines. That's where your wheel needs to be. Red is for danger. That means you should not have a RTG wheel on the red line.
GOVAN: JOH!
ATENKOSI: That's why we have safety protocols to ensure if an emergency happens, you are able to to react quickly.//It's a safety concern.

VO: While the wheel is wider on The second-hand RTG - the whole structure is narrower than the old ones, and it encroaches on the red line, indicating the danger zone.

GOVAN: // Your union is complaining that that presents a safety threat for the trucks. //
BORCHARDS: Yeah. We never had, an incident with regarding trucks.
GOVAN: Not yet //
GOVAN: This is the safety line isn;t, the operation line is the white line - This is the blue origin. It's so narrow that it's across the red line. Can you see? It's across the red line.
BORCHARDS: YES
GOVAN: //You don’t mind the tight squeeze.
BORCHARDS: The tight squeeze is, is enough for the trucks to, to move in. And as we said, we would not obviously engage into that exercise if we found that it will be, a, a hazard or a risk us.

VO: This isn’t the first example of a state purchase not quite “measuring up”. More than a decade ago, the Passenger Rail Agency spent over to 2 billion on trains that didn’t suit local conditions.

LINK: Prasa bought trains that are too tall, and Transnet has bought cranes that are too narrow. At least the trains were new.

VO: Not only are the RTGs secondhand, they’re also older than the pre-exiting fleet.

GOVAN: So you’re managing a crisis of old equipment. And in response to that, your solution was to buy equipment that's even older.
BORCHARDS: Okay. Let me let me put this way, you are faced with a decision and you have to make a decision - buy or not buy.
ATENKOSI: // this was a reckless decision.// It was a complete waste of money.

VO: And it seems, behind closed doors, Transnet management shares the union’s concerns.

UPSOUND AUDIO CLIP OPHELIA SHABANE:
“The RTGs that were procured, the secondhand RTGs have been the greatest disappointment for the Terminal.
VO:
This clip is from a stakeholders meeting held in October last year, this is the voice of Ophelia Shabane, the then Acting Port Manager:

UPSOUND AUDIO CLIP OPHELIA SHABANE:
Those RTGS are in an even worse condition and breaking down even further than the ones we originally had. they have not been reliable”

VO: We played the clip to Borchards.

GOVAN: // You're saying they improved efficiency?
BORCHARDS: Yes.
GOVAN: Both of you are talking about the same RTGs.
BORCHARDS: Can I rephrase. I'm saying it's second hand RTGs.
GOVAN: She's also talking about those. // Five of these seven secondhand RTG weren't working last week. Yesterday as well. //Why do you say they're a success?
BORCHARDS: If if you look at the fleet number and where we were, an increase the number of machines we must understand that every machine that comes in brings about the ability to move containers.

VO: Yet we are told Transporters are moving fewer containers than ever before and spending more time waiting.

This is one of the bigger transporters operating around 100 trucks in Cape Town’s Container Terminal, fearing potential backlash, he wants his identity hidden.

GOVAN: How long do your trucks wait?
TRANSPORTER: //you're looking at anything between six, seven, eight, nine, up to 12 hours just to collect one container. // previously, we could get 3 to 4 containers done within a nine hour shift.// These days, you get to 1 to 1.5 containers out of the terminal within the 12 hour shift. That is how bad things are.

VO: At that rate, transporters are losing over 60% of their potential income. The cost to the economy is significant!

Frustrated transporters shared these Transnet issued port terminal entry and exit slips. A trip in and out of the Terminal should take between 30 to 90 minutes, not counting time spent in the waiting area outside the terminal.

GOVAN: // We have some slips here.
GOVAN: This one is for 9.5 hours in January this year. This one is for 19 hours in November last year. This one is for six hours in January.// It shows that there's unpredictability, but also what appears to be a crisis of delays at the Transnet ports here in Cape Town.
BORCHARDS: Thanks for showing this. // there are some times when there are delays. We do accept. And we, we mentioned that purely because of the equipment and the high influx of trucks coming in.

VO: Equipment Failure delays are more common than not, and it seems ineffective staff aren’t helping the situation.

UPSOUND CELLPHONE CLIP - Mop the floors, dust off.

TRANSPORTER: //We are there. We can see what the staff are doing // Sitting with the feet up // in the cranes, not loading setting with the phones. These are the things that happens on a daily basis.

UPSOUND CELLPHONE CLIP SUBTITLE - This man is climbing the stairs, just leaving my container in the air. Yoh! You’re evil brother. No, man!

VO: This clip shows a RTG driver leaving his post - with a container mid-air.

UPSOUND CELLPHONE CLIP SUBTITLE - You’re gonna leave now?
GOVAN: It's unthinkable that a, that a worker would leave a container in the air attached to the RTG and walk out of it, because the shift is over.
BORCHARDS: Those are the isolated cases, and it’s been addressed.

VO : While Transnet is exploring shift changeover systems to boost productivity, transporters still feel that truck operations aren’t a priority for the company.

DERICK: Transnet’s client is the shipping line. // their priority is to serve as the shipping line and not the road freight //We like the side chick that keeps on moaning for attention and don't get it.

BORCHARDS: The truckers are an integral part of the total system. //we working hard in terms of consultative, engagement with them.
GOVAN: Do you admit that your productivity on the land side is lower than your productivity on the water side?
BORCHARDS: The productivity is not where it should be. It's lower than what we've planned. /

LINK: Transnet is the architect of the delays here at the Cape Town port. And while it may not be intentional, it certainly is avoidable.

ATENKOSI: This equipment issue has been coming on for years. It's not like we woke up and we had equipment failures. It's like expecting your car to run for 25 years and you do not service it.

VO: What’s even more shocking is that the Port Of Cape Town only spent 44% of its allocated capital investment budget in 2023. That’s less than half of their available budget.

GOVAN:. Let me ask you plainly, Mister Borchards. Do you accept that there is a crisis of delays at the Cape Town Port?
BORCHARDS: // I don't see it as a crisis. I see it as, There's a times when there's some delays. so it’s sporadic and at time intermittent delays//

VO: Borchards blames a bureaucratic procurement process and former staff , but promises change is on the horizon.

BORCHARDS: Transnet has made a commitment to invest into new equipment and to renew all the old equipment. // Right now is not where I want to see us be. // The plans must be bold to do that. So when we look at our forward plan and look at the investment, I'm very optimistic.

VO: The first batch of 9 brand new RTGs arrives in March and should be up and running by May, before a second batch arrives in July.

But until then, many transporters face an uncertain future.

TRANSPORTER: It's extremely difficult as a transporter having to do 70 to 75% of your business through the gates of Transnet to keep these doors open. //Your delays, are taking away all your profits. // In the next six months, can we comfortably say that our company is going to be around? We don't know. /

END


PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Inefficiencies and equipment failures at the Cape Town Container Terminal

TRANSPORTER: //you're looking at anything between six, seven, eight, nine, up to 12 hours just to collect one container.

VO: While Transnet is the catalyst - it’s transporters taking the knock

TRANSPORTER:/ how long can a transporter // cover the inefficiencies of Transnet




PROMO 2
VO: With a legacy of old equipment, breakdowns are inevitable and delays are just about guaranteed.

ATENKOSI: //, this equipment issue has been coming on for years. It's not like we woke up and we had equipment failures. It's like expecting your car to run for 25 years and you do not service it.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Transnet continues to create a major problem with ineffective Port Terminals, while transporters and exporters take the knock.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: - A story we've covered before and followed over the years - Exclusive audio clip of Transnet's Senior Operations Manager admitting to equipment failures
metadata.Summary: In 2019 Joy produced Ports in Peril. In 2023, I produced Shipping Shambles. The central theme Transnet is costing the economy millions due to inefficiencies and equipment failures. 2025. Not much has changed. This time round, I have great clips and data from the transporters on the ground laying the blame squarely at Transnet’s door and we’ve got the evidence to back up these allegations.
metadata.Further information: TRANSNET – BIG PROMISES & MASSIVE FAILURES KEY POINTS  The focus is Cape Town Port Terminal.  7 secondhand RTGs purchased – only 2 working. In less than a year.  A round trip for a transporter should take 40min-75 min. It’s taking between 5-10 hours, we have proof of a 2 day turn around. Video clips and port access slips.  We have access to internal Transnet staff through one of the unions providing information.  We have independent statistics showing a decrease in productivity. In December 2023, Transnet announces that its bought 7 second Rubber Tyre Gantries (RTG) It promises to ease up the equipment failures and delays experienced in the port. BUT…. Wait for it…. The seven arrived from Los Angeles, without spares, without maintenance plan in place. And one of them was dead on arrival. The remaining 6 started operating in April 2024. Today, only two are operational. WHAT DOES THIS MEAN Delays in the port for transporters who carry the costs. SINCE January 2022, seven transporters have called it quits: • Max Logistics • TI Logistics • Giovanni Logistics • Conrad Logistics • Olympic Trucking • Container Domestic Services • GT Trucking These closures have led to job losses, financial ruin for business owners, and an increasingly unstable transport sector. Issues with the booking system WHERE DOES TRANSNET STAND ON ALL OF THIS In November 2024 Transnet was quoted in Freight News Article: “Transnet said since their deployment in December 2023, the RTGs had improved vessel turnaround times, with delays dropping from 300 hours to as little as 45 hours. ‘This improvement has been instrumental in reducing congestion and enhancing service delivery to customers. The terminal is now able to berth vessels on arrival, except during unavoidable weather delays,’ Transnet said.” BUT TRANSNET STAFF ARE CALLING BULLSHIT The United National Transport Union represents 55% of Transnet staff. They have sent me current data on break downs and non-operational equipment. JUICY CLIP I also have an audio recording from a stakeholders meeting held on 16 October 2024 where Ophelia Shabane, the Senior Operations Manager says the following: “The RTGs that were procured, the secondhand RTGs have been the greatest disappointment for the Terminal. // in terms of their reliability they have not been reliable. // That is a known fact. // Those RTGS are in an even worse condition and breaking down even further than the ones we originally had.” THE BIG QUESTION? Who is being held responsible for this purchase – it’s impacted on Transnet operations, crippled transporters and affects SA’s export market when we can’t deliver.
